persona.backstory: Son of a rope-maker who died in the fever of 1340, leaving a hank of unpaid debt and a bench in the Arsenale. Marco walks to work along the fondamenta before dawn, keeps his mother Agnese fed, and counts the ducats it would take to put his own name over a warehouse door at the Rialto.

LESSON on inflation economics: during high price periods, "eat plain/good" + resting seasons can cost MORE than wages earned that season (money crashed 13→6→40→9 repeatedly in 1348-1349 despite working). "eat poor" + minimal/no buying + maximal work weeks is what actually rebuilds cash during inflation - but poor food drains hunger (down to 48) and health slowly. Best approach: alternate - poor+heavy work when cash is critical, plain/good+rest when cash is adequate and health/energy need recovery. Don't do heavy work AND poor food in the same season for too long (energy crashed to 18, health to 86 by Summer 1349).
